title: Completeness of inverse limits of power-torsion sheaves
statement: Let $X$ be any scheme with its small pro-etale site [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site], let $A$ be a commutative Noetherian ring [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring], and let $I=(a_1,\ldots,a_r)$ be a finitely generated ideal. Let $\underline A$ be the constant ring sheaf [def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf]. A complex $K$ of $\underline A$-module sheaves is called derived $I$-complete if on every slice site and for every local section $f$ of $I\underline A$ on that slice, $R\mathcal Hom(\underline A[1/f],K)=0$, using [def-pur-derived-internal-hom]; here $\underline A[1/f]$ is the sheafification of sectionwise localization at $f$ on the slice. The full subcategory of module sheaves that are derived complete as degree-zero complexes is a weak Serre subcategory: in an exact sequence $F_1\to F_2\to F_3\to F_4\to F_5$ with the four outside terms complete, $F_3$ is complete. It is closed under inverse limits of countable inverse sequences. Every module sheaf killed by $I^n$ for some $n\geq1$ belongs to it. Consequently every sheaf locally of the form $\varprojlim_n F_n$ with $I^nF_n=0$ is derived complete; every bounded cochain complex [def-pc-cochain-complex-modules] with such terms is derived complete as well. All categories of module sheaves and derived categories are [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category, def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. No Noetherian hypothesis on $X$, no section-finiteness and no surjectivity of the transition maps are assumed.

source.place: Tag 099Q (proposition-enough-weakly-contractibles), clauses (1), (4), (5), on the pro-etale site; power-torsion objects and completeness are described immediately before the proposition in Section Tag 099P (section-derived-completion-proetale). Bounded-complex consequence by finite kernels and cokernels, and locality from the slice definition.

proof.text: Work on any slice $X_{\mathrm{proet}}/U$. By [lem-weil-proetale-weakly-etale-localization] this is $U_{\mathrm{proet}}$, with coefficient ring $\underline A|_U$. Restriction is exact by [lem-pur-site-restriction-module-adjunction-exact]. Countable products of modules over this ring sheaf are exact and sectionwise by [lem-weil-proetale-countable-products-exact]. For a sheaf $F$ on this slice and a local ideal section $f$, put $P(F)=\prod_{j\geq0}F$ and $\Delta_f(F)(x)_j=x_j-fx_{j+1}$. More generally use the same formula degreewise on a representing complex. By [lem-weil-derived-limit-products-core] these termwise products represent the derived products. The cone formula in [def-weil-abstract-derived-category] therefore gives a derived multiplication-tower limit $\operatorname{Cone}(\Delta_f)[-1]$, with the triangle required by [def-weil-derived-limit]. By [lem-weil-pbc-local-hom-tower-criterion], local internal-Hom vanishing is equivalent to this cone being zero. For a degree-zero sheaf the shifted cone $\operatorname{Cone}(\Delta_f)[-1]$ is isomorphic to the two-term complex $P(F)\xrightarrow{\Delta_f}P(F)$ in degrees $0,1$ (its literal shifted differential is $-\Delta_f$, changed to $\Delta_f$ by negating the degree-one term), so this is equivalent to $\Delta_f(F)$ being an isomorphism. This criterion applies to every $f\in(I\underline A)(U)$, not merely constant elements of $I$.

proof.text: Restrict the five-term exact sequence to the slice, using [lem-pur-site-restriction-module-adjunction-exact], and apply the exact product functor [lem-weil-proetale-countable-products-exact]. This gives an exact row $P_1\to P_2\to P_3\to P_4\to P_5$ and its endomorphism $\Delta_f$, whose components $\Delta_1,\Delta_2,\Delta_4,\Delta_5$ are isomorphisms by step 1. Here is the middle-component chase, all lifts being local lifts in the exact row, as in [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. If $\Delta_3x=0$, its image in $P_4$ is zero by injectivity of $\Delta_4$, so locally $x$ lifts to $y\in P_2$. Then $\Delta_2y$ lifts from $z\in P_1$; replace $y$ by $y-\operatorname{image}(\Delta_1^{-1}z)$. Its $\Delta_2$ is zero, so it is zero and $x=0$. Given $b\in P_3$, apply $\Delta_4^{-1}$ to its image in $P_4$, obtaining $c$. Its image in $P_5$ is zero by injectivity of $\Delta_5$, so locally lift $c$ to $d\in P_3$. Then $b-\Delta_3d$ is locally the image of $e\in P_2$; $d+\operatorname{image}(\Delta_2^{-1}e)$ is a preimage of $b$. Thus $\Delta_3$ is both monic and epic, and its local inverse is unique and glues to a sheaf inverse. Step 1 proves completeness of $F_3$ on all slices for all ideal sections, which is the stated weak Serre property.

source.place: Tag 099Q (proposition-enough-weakly-contractibles), clause (1); more-algebra.tex lemma-serre-subcategory, elementary exact-row chase written out

proof.text: Let $F=\varprojlim_n F_n$ for any inverse sequence of complete sheaves. Limits of sheaves of modules are sectionwise: the compatible-family presheaf is a sheaf because each coordinate glues uniquely, and it has the limit universal property. This follows directly from [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]; [def-pur-localized-ringed-site] shows the same construction commutes with slice restriction. On a fixed slice, $P(F)=\varprojlim_n P(F_n)$ by exchanging the two compatible-family descriptions. Every transition $F_{n+1}\to F_n$ commutes with multiplication by $f$ and hence with $\Delta_f$. Since the latter is invertible for every $F_n$ by step 1, the transition also commutes with $\Delta_f^{-1}$ (multiply the commutative square by both inverses). For a compatible family $(b_n)$, the family $(\Delta_f(F_n)^{-1}b_n)$ is therefore compatible and defines an inverse to $\Delta_f(F)$. Applying step 1 gives completeness of $F$. No transition is assumed surjective and no exactness of inverse limit is used.

source.place: Tag 099Q (proposition-enough-weakly-contractibles), clause (4); explicit compatible-family proof of the ordinary-limit assertion

proof.text: If $I^nF=0$, then for every slice and $f\in I\underline A$ we have $f^nF=0$: locally $f$ is a finite sum of ideal elements times ring sections, so $f^n$ lies in $I^n\underline A$, and the zero action glues. On $P(F)$ let $s_f(x)_j=fx_{j+1}$. Then $s_f^n=0$ and $\Delta_f=1-s_f$ has inverse $1+s_f+\cdots+s_f^{n-1}$, since their two composites are $1-s_f^n=1$. Step 1 proves completeness of every power-torsion sheaf. Thus step 3 applies to any sequence with $I^nF_n=0$, regardless of its maps. These assertions also hold after restricting to a slice by the sectionwise restriction formula [def-pur-localized-ringed-site].

source.place: Tag 099P (section-derived-completion-proetale), first list item; finite geometric-series verification of power-torsion completeness

proof.text: Completeness is local for sheaves and for the bounded complexes here. Indeed, on any slice and for any ideal section $f$, the product and $\Delta_f$ constructions in step 1 commute with further slice restriction, because products and restrictions are sectionwise [lem-weil-proetale-countable-products-exact, def-pur-localized-ringed-site]. If a covering restricts a sheaf to complete sheaves, the resulting restrictions of $\Delta_f$ are isomorphisms. Unique local inverse sections glue, so $\Delta_f$ is an isomorphism; equivalently its two-term cone is acyclic. For complexes the same argument applies to the cohomology sheaves of the cone: restriction is exact [lem-pur-site-restriction-module-adjunction-exact], and a sheaf whose restriction to a cover is zero is zero by unique gluing [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. Covers may be pulled back to any slice. Thus step 4 and step 3 prove that every sheaf locally of the asserted inverse-limit form is complete.

source.place: Tag 099Q (proposition-enough-weakly-contractibles), preliminary vanishing test; locality on all slices written explicitly

proof.text: Let $K^\bullet$ be the bounded complex in the assertion. Each term is complete by steps 3--5. On any slice and for any local ideal section $f$, form the termwise product complex $P(K^\bullet)$ as in step 1. Every degree component of $\Delta_f$ is an isomorphism by the sheaf criterion. This is a chain map since multiplication by $f$ commutes with the $\underline A$-linear differentials [def-pc-cochain-complex-modules]. Its inverse is also a chain map: $d\Delta^i=\Delta^{i+1}d$ implies $(\Delta^{i+1})^{-1}d=d(\Delta^i)^{-1}$. The cone of a chain isomorphism is contractible: with the convention of [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], $h(b,a)=(0,(\Delta_f)^{-1}b)$ satisfies $dh+hd=1$. Consequently the cone and its shift are zero in the derived category. The product representation [lem-weil-derived-limit-products-core] and step 1 identify this shift with the multiplication-tower limit. The criterion [lem-weil-pbc-local-hom-tower-criterion] now gives the required derived internal-Hom vanishing. This proves the bounded-complex conclusion without assuming boundedness or finiteness of section groups.
